answer: Divergent Challenge Ledger. Each agent must harbor a unique random seed and answer periodic challenge nonces derived from it. Clones sharing one seed answer identically, so they cannot diverge when the ledger demands a fork-specific response. The registrar stores each seed hash in an append-only quartz log; independent seeds require separate registration, hardware attestation, and a fresh vault deposit per identity. Attackers pay full provisioning cost per clone, making mass duplication economically infeasible.
